transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO, AtlasCommerce), Meera (ML), Jordan (Product), Tess (Infra)

Summary:
Quick sync to review this week's pilot results, dig into a failing function-calling flow, clarify acceptance criteria for the POC, and schedule a connectivity/benchmark run for dedicated/private test. Some discussion about latency vs batch sizing and structured output stability.

Topics:
- Latest results from sandbox integration
- Failure reproduction for function-calling (tool invocation mismatch)
- Acceptance criteria for go/no-go for pilot
- Security/connectivity checklist for private sandbox
- Next steps and owners

Action items (also in metadata): see list

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: All right, hey everyone, welcome. uh thanks for carving out time today, we wanted to go over the recent test runs you sent and a couple of the failing cases Meera flagged.
[00:18] Liam: Thanks, Sofia, yeah we got some pretty weird output when we tried to call the inventory update tool, it spat back this sort of malformed JSON and then the SDK crashed.
[00:30] Ethan: Got it, do you have a quick sample? if you can paste one into the shared doc that's ideal. I think Meera put a snippet in the sheet?
[00:42] Meera: yeah I uploaded 3 examples under "failed-invokes.csv" — the first one is the most common, it's when the tool returns a 200 but the body wraps the function result in an extra layer. so Redwood's function-caller doesn't match the schema.
[00:58] Priya: okay that sounds like a schema mismatch; are you using the SDK wrapper or direct REST calls?
[01:06] Meera: SDK, Node 18 with the Redwood client. We saw the same with curl though when simulating the payload.
[01:14] Ethan: interesting. our SDK expects the tool response to be unwrapped in the function response field — in some custom tool chains they wrap again for internal reasons. we can add a tolerant parsing mode on our end to accept an extra outer field.
[01:29] Jordan: is that something we can toggle per-route? atlas doesn't want a global permissive mode for other flows.
[01:37] Sofia: good call, per-route toggle is the right ask — that maps to the Redwood route config we showed earlier. we'll check if it's fine to add a "lenient_function_parsing" flag to the route.
[01:46] Liam: timeline wise, we need a fix or a workaround before we run the acceptance benchmark, otherwise the timers are skewed by retries.
[01:54] Ethan: understood. quick workaround: the pilot orchestration can insert a preprocessor lambda to unwrap the payload client-side. but longer term we push a small SDK patch.
[02:06] Tess: sorry to interrupt — on the sandbox VPC test, we still need a firewall rule to allow egress to the Redwood sandbox IP range. I've put a note in the cart.
[02:17] Sofia: thanks Tess, that's in the action items. we'll coordinate on the ports.
[02:22] Meera: back to the function calling, one of the failed cases had a mis-typed param name — product_id vs productId — which caused the tool to respond with an error text blob instead of structured JSON.
[02:34] Priya: ah okay so two orthogonal issues: param naming mismatch and wrapper layer. good to surface both.
[02:41] [03:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible) can you also confirm the tokenization mismatch? we saw prompts that produce wildly different token counts between the open-source tokenizers.
[03:12] Ethan: yeah that's expected; different tokenizers — especially with modern subword rules — will produce variance. we recommend counting tokens via the Redwood SDK token_count util to ensure consistent batching.
[03:24] Jordan: for acceptance criteria, we proposed 95th percentile latency < 250ms for single-turn checkout prompts at 256 tokens and failure rate < 1% on function invokes. is that achievable?
[03:36] Ethan: 250ms 95th at 256 tokens is tight on hosted mode unless you tune batching. on Dedicated it's much more feasible. we should baseline current numbers.
[03:46] Meera: what were the numbers from last week's run? I saw a spreadsheet but it had a couple of weird outliers.
[03:54] Sofia: quick summary: median token latency ~120ms, p95 around 380ms on sandbox (no dedicated), with a few retries pushing p99 above a second. throughput was fine but the function-call retry loop amplified tail latency.
[04:12] Ethan: key root cause for the tail was synchronous blocking on cold KV cache fills for a subset of product prompts — KV cache cold-start added ~200-300ms in some traces.
[04:23] Meera: KV cache — I'm pretty sure their infra team mis-configured the TTL, it's rehydrating too often.
[04:29] Tess: right we had some TTL set at 30s during dev, should be 24h for the shape of this workload.
[04:36] Priya: changing TTL will definitely reduce cold starts. also Redwood has an optional prefix caching mode that keeps commonly requested KV warm across requests, we can enable that in the route.
[04:47] [05:00] Liam: ok lets enumerate acceptance tests then: correctness of structured output (schema match for tool calls), p95 latency below 300ms on sandbox baseline (with routing/batching tuned), and successful run of a 5k-record batch ingestion with no crashes.
[05:12] Ethan: for the 5k ingestion can you clarify concurrency — do you want single-client sequential or parallel clients?
[05:20] Jordan: parallel 16 clients to simulate real traffic at our peak.
[05:25] Ethan: noted. we'll run throughput tests at 16 concurrency and provide token-per-second and error rate breakdown.
[05:31] Meera: also need to ensure embeddings calls for search don't regress — we saw a 10% delta in similarity scores after switching quantized model variant.
[05:40] Priya: oh that's important. Redwood Optimize suggested a q4_0f16 profile for the CPU/GPU mix; quantization can change embeddings subtlely. we should lock an embed model for the POC and run A/B evaluation.
[05:52] [06:00] Meera: yes let's do that, we need stable semantic similarity above threshold not just speed.
[06:06] Ethan: we'll run an embeddings regression test: same prompt set, compare cosine similarity distribution, and flag any median drop > 2 points.
[06:16] Jordan: how will we surface that in the console? we need a dashboard tile for embedding drift.
[06:22] Sofia: we can add a temporary dashboard with the A/B comparisons and daily alerts. not full product GA but enough for POC.
[06:30] Tess: one more infra note — for the private test we will need KMS key ownership questions answered, does Redwood support our HSM-backed key?
[06:40] Sofia: yes, for Private we support external KMS/HSM integrations, you'll need to provision a key and we can show the flow. I'll attach the integration guide.
[06:49] Liam: can we get a short whitepaper on compliance — SOC2 details and audit logs for how inference requests are logged?
[06:57] Sofia: absolutely, I will send SOC2 summary and sample audit log schema.
[07:03] [07:30] Speaker 2 (Meera): re the function-calling patch, what's the expected turnaround?
[07:38] Ethan: SDK patch for tolerant parse — we can do an internal build in 3 business days, public NPM release maybe 7 days if no regressions.
[07:46] Meera: great. if you can also provide a quick manual mitigation in the orchestration we can keep testing meanwhile.
[07:54] Priya: on that point, the manual unwrapping preprocessor is a one-liner in the middleware; we'll paste it in the doc after the meeting.
[08:02] Jordan: about the schema tests — what do you need from us to validate?
[08:07] Ethan: sample schema JSON and 50 representative sample outputs that constitute golden examples. we'll write a test harness that asserts structural equivalence and field presence.
[08:16] Meera: I'll upload those tonight.
[08:18] Tess: on VPC connectivity, do you need a public IP for the sandbox endpoint or can we do NAT through our egress?
[08:25] Sofia: Redwood's sandbox supports both — if you want outbound NAT that's fine, we only need to allow the IP ranges; we'll share the list.
[08:33] [09:00] Liam: slightly broader question: if we hit production scale and need to move to Dedicated, what's the migration effort?
[09:08] Sofia: migration is a config and routing change in most cases; Dedicated provides reserved GPUs, SLA, and more predictable p95. you'll have to plan a small downtime window for model pinning but code-level changes are minimal if you use the SDK.
[09:22] Ethan: also note that some quantized model variants behave differently on different hardware; we'll help tune those profiles during migration.
[09:32] Meera: ok good.
[09:35] Jordan: one thing — we saw more hallucinations in structured outputs when we push system prompt temperature up to 0.6 for creativity. acceptance needs to account for that tradeoff.
[09:46] Priya: yep, we recommend keeping temperature at 0.2 for transactional flows and use sampling only in non-critical UX. we'll document recommended param profiles.
[09:55] [10:30] Speaker 1: (typing) are we going to attach the benchmark runner?
[10:34] Ethan: yes we'll attach the benchmark runner to the shared drive along with a README — it's a node/python hybrid.
[10:40] Meera: small nit — the runner uses a different tokenizer lib by default, can you make sure token counts match our prod tokenizer?
[10:48] Ethan: we'll align tokenizers; I'll add a tokenization shim.
[10:53] Sofia: ok, let's recap next steps: Redwood sends benchmark script and SDK patch; Atlas sends sample prompts and schema; infra coordinates VPC egress; schedule a 2-hr run next week. any other blockers?
[11:07] Liam: no blockers, just timeline sensitivity. we want the pilot acceptance run by 2026-07-15 if possible.
[11:14] Sofia: sounds reasonable, we'll target that.
[11:18] Jordan: last question — cost estimate for Dedicated for our peak throughput? we need a ballpark for planning.
[11:24] Sofia: I'll include a high-level pricing estimate in the follow-up email — committed GPU pools pricing and an estimated per-token delta vs hosted.
[11:31] Meera: and include any options for auto-burst vs overprovisioning.
[11:36] Sofia: yup.
[11:38] [12:00] Tess: thanks everyone, we'll sync on firewall rules off-band.
[12:04] Ethan: I'll start the benchmark runs once we have the sample set.
[12:08] Sofia: great, thanks both teams. We'll follow up with the artifacts.

Links / shared artifacts referenced:
- sandbox-results.csv (attached in shared folder)
- failed-invokes.csv (Meera)
- benchmark-runner (node/python) link — will be posted in the follow-up
- security packet + SOC2 summary (Sofia to attach)

End of meeting.
